title: Research
text:
My research focuses on quantitative defect spectroscopy and experimental data analysis for two-dimensional (2D) materials and oxide semiconductors.
I aim to extract physically meaningful parameters from electrical and optical measurements and connect them to material properties and device behavior. Interpretability and reproducibility are central to this work.

1. Defect & Optical Spectroscopy

Quantitative analysis of intrinsic and extrinsic defects in 2D materials and oxide semiconductors.
Extraction of defect energy levels, densities, and carrier dynamics using DLTS and PICTS.
Raman and photoluminescence (PL) spectroscopy for probing defect states, doping, strain, and phase transitions.
XPS and spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) for chemical composition, bonding states, and optical properties.
Tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) for spatially resolved analysis of defects and structural inhomogeneity beyond the diffraction limit.



2. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) for Experimental Data

Development of analysis pipelines for spectroscopic and electrical datasets, including preprocessing, feature extraction, modeling, and validation.
Use of XAI to identify physically relevant features in the data.
Connection of AI-extracted features to defect-related mechanisms and material properties under data-limited experimental conditions.



3. Advanced Electronic & Photonic Devices

Fabrication and characterization of electronic devices based on 2D materials and oxide semiconductors, including logic and neuromorphic devices.
Quantitative analysis of device electrical responses (e.g., I–V characteristics and transient behavior) to identify dominant transport and trapping mechanisms.
FDTD simulations of optical responses and electric-field distributions in structures ranging from the nanoscale to the microscale, supporting the design and analysis of photonic components.
